summary: Global foundations that every component builds on: border-box sizing, a dependable `[hidden]`, body typography, the fixed dot-grid backdrop, resets for links, buttons, form controls and SVGs, the aqua keyboard focus ring, small utility classes (`.mono`, `.num`, `.muted`, `.dim`, `.faint`, `.eyebrow`) and dark scrollbars. It ends with the motion kill-switch, which honours both the operating system's reduced-motion setting and the app's own `data-motion` toggle.

notes.text: Makes every element, plus its `::before` and `::after` pseudo-elements, use `border-box` sizing, so a declared width or height already includes padding and border. Sizes written in the stylesheets (a 34px button, a 13px spectrum dot) are therefore exactly what appears on screen.

Guarantees that the HTML `hidden` attribute always hides. The browser's built-in `display: none` for `[hidden]` loses to any author rule that sets `display` (such as `.drawer { display: flex }`), so `!important` makes `el.hidden = true` in JS dependable for the drawer, palette, boot screen, new-events pill and incident count badge.
Stops mobile Safari from automatically enlarging text when the phone is rotated to landscape, so the type scale stays as designed.

Page-wide defaults: no default margin, at least the full viewport height, the darkest surface as background and the primary text colour. The `font` shorthand sets a compact 13.5px Geist at regular weight with a 1.5 line height; `font-feature-settings` turns on two optional Geist glyph alternates (stylistic set 01 and character variant 11), `-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased` makes light-on-dark text look crisper and less heavy on macOS, and `overflow-x: hidden` prevents a horizontal scrollbar if anything ends up wider than the viewport.

The decorative backdrop behind the app (the empty `.backdrop` div at the top of `index.html`). It is fixed to the viewport, ignores the pointer and sits at `z-index: 0` beneath the shell; its background layers a large, faint aqua glow centred just above the top edge (72% across) over a tiled dot grid, a 1px dot in every 22px tile. The mask, repeated with a `-webkit-` prefix for Safari, fades the whole layer from full strength at the top to 35% at mid-screen and to nothing at the bottom.
Links inherit the surrounding text colour and drop the underline, because in this UI every link is styled by its own class (nav item, button or ID link).
Browsers give form controls their own system font instead of inheriting it, so this makes buttons, inputs, selects and textareas use the page's Geist font, size and text colour.
Strips the native button look (background, border and padding) so each component class styles its buttons from a blank slate, and gives every button a pointer cursor.
SVGs are inline by default, which leaves a small gap under them for text descenders; `display: block` removes it so icons align exactly inside flex and grid layouts.
Text highlighted with the mouse gets a soft aqua background instead of the browser's default blue, keeping even the selection on-palette.

The keyboard focus ring: a 2px aqua outline drawn 2px outside the element. `:focus-visible` only matches when the browser decides focus should be shown (typically keyboard navigation), so mouse clicks don't flash rings, and the small radius rounds the ring on elements that don't set their own corners.

`.mono` switches to Geist Mono for data such as IDs, IPs and scores. The `"zero"` feature turns on the font's alternate zero, which is marked so it can't be confused with the letter O in IDs like `EVT-00001`, and a tiny negative letter-spacing tightens the wide monospace glyphs.
`.num` switches to tabular (equal-width) digits, so numbers line up in columns and animated counters don't jitter sideways as their digits change.

Text-colour utilities that step down the grey ramp: `.muted` uses `--t2`, `.dim` uses `--t3` and `.faint` uses `--t4`. The JS templates add them to tone down secondary details such as locations, timestamps and empty values.

`.eyebrow` is the small label above page titles, nav groups and KPI values (for example "Events · 24h"): 10.5px medium Geist Mono, uppercase, widely letter-spaced and in `--t3`. It gives the dashboard a technical, editorial feel without adding colour.

Custom scrollbars for Chromium and Safari (Firefox ignores these `::-webkit-` pseudo-elements and shows its own dark scrollbar thanks to `color-scheme: dark`). Bars are 10px, the thumb is an `--s4` pill whose 3px border in the page colour makes it look slimmer and floating, and the track is transparent.
Comment, then the start of a media query that applies only when the user has turned on "reduce motion" in their operating system's accessibility settings.

Inside it, every element and pseudo-element gets 0.01ms animations and transitions with a single iteration, forced with `!important` so no component rule can override it. A near-zero duration instead of `animation: none` still lets everything land in its final state (and fire its end events), while infinite loops such as the live-dot ping and the border beam stop moving.

The same kill-switch for the app's own setting: motion.js sets `data-motion="off"` on the `html` element when the user picks "Reduce motion" in the command palette, and remembers the choice in localStorage. anime.js animations are skipped separately through `motionEnabled()`, so CSS and JS motion switch off together.
